learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate explains fundamental notions of energy, exergy, and anergy.
The student/graduate describes principles of energy and exergetic balances for open and closed systems.
The student/graduate identifies main mechanisms of energetic and exergetic losses in thermal-mechanical installations.
The student/graduate explains relationships between energetic, exergetic analysis, and thermodynamic performances.
The student/graduate knows the methodology for developing complex balances for industrial systems.
The student/graduate uses analytical methods and specialized software for calculating energy and exergetic balances.
The student/graduate develops energetic and exergetic diagrams for components such as: heat exchangers, turbines, compressors, engines, industrial installations.
The student/graduate evaluates system performance based on energetic and exergetic indicators.
The student/graduate identifies solutions for energetic and exergetic optimization by reducing irreversibilities.
The student/graduate critically interprets technical data and experimental results.
The student/graduate respects ethical and professional principles regarding technical analysis and reporting results.
The student/graduate takes responsibility for the correct use of calculation tools.
The student/graduate integrates energetic, exergetic, and sustainability criteria into engineering decisions.
The student/graduate works efficiently in multidisciplinary teams.
The student/graduate develops autonomy in documentation and in applying modern analysis methods.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to energetic and exergetic analysis: Notions of energy, exergy, anergy
Differences between energetic and exergetic analysis
Relevance of balances in mechanical engineering
Energetic balances for open and closed systems: Fundamental equations
Energy transfer through work and heat
Application of balances in simple installations
Fundamentals of exergy and exergetic balances: Physical and chemical exergy
General equation of the exergetic balance
Analysis of irreversibilities and identification of losses: Exergy destruction
Evaluation of energetic and exergetic efficiency: Performance indicators
Complex balances for thermal and industrial systems: Systems with multiple exchange zones
Energetic and exergetic optimization. Applied examples: Multicriteria methods
Establishing initial data and system modeling: Defining the analyzed system
Drawing up the energetic balance: Calculating energy flows
Drawing up the exergetic balance: Determining exergy of flows
Analysis of results and system optimization: Synthesis of energetic and exergetic balances
teaching_methods: Interpretation of results obtained in exercises or simulations

assessment_methods.method: Examination/Verification (including systematic observation, individual/team assignments, formative and summative evaluation tests)
Project (including documentation, project activity, finalization, and presentation)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Integer grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded. A grade of 5 certifies the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its associated study credits.
